# Acceptance review: Attendance unavailable/denied card (c0a98bf → candidate)

This was a read-only review: I looked at all six images and the source and CSS you pasted. I changed no files and ran nothing.

## Source verdict: PASS

- **Unavailable branch** (any error other than `42501`): the card has the `h2`, a message, and the existing same-page reload link. That link's class changed from `secondary-button` to `primary-button`, and its `href` is still the same page. The single "back to workspace" link stays outside the card as `secondary-button`. That leaves one main action and one way out, so there's no dead end.
- **Denied branch** (`42501`): the card shows the heading and the permission reason only. There is no retry link, so it doesn't offer a recovery that can't work, and the "back to workspace" link still shows. This is consistent with your authority rules.
- **Valid snapshot branch**: `MobilePunch`, the history list, review decisions, the time-zone fallback and the HR note are as in your excerpt. No Auth, RPC, redirect or storage logic is involved.
- **CSS**: the four selectors are all scoped under `.channel-page .channel-read-state`. They set only padding, grid gap, heading margin/size/weight, paragraph margin/line-height, and `justify-self` on the in-card link. Nothing changes colour, width, layout outside the card, or behaviour. `clamp(1rem, 2.5vw, 1.5rem)` matches the measured padding: 16px at 390, 19.2px at 768, 24px at 1366.
- I accept your exact-inversion and prefix claims on the strength of your report. I did not re-hash the files.

## Scoped visual verdict: MATCH WITH ACCEPTED DEVIATIONS

- **Before (light mobile)**: the text sits against the card edge, and the reload link is cramped against the copy and styled like the outer "back to workspace" link. That confirms the baseline defect.
- **After (light mobile)**: the card now has padding, a clear heading, a 1.7 line height, and the teal primary reload button aligned to the start (right in RTL). "Back to workspace" stays secondary, and its visible focus ring shows that keyboard focus is shown.
- **After (dark desktop)**: the hierarchy is the same, with the dark card, teal primary button and outlined secondary button. This matches the reference's dark palette, its 8px-radius cards with stronger borders, and its Cairo-family type.
- **Denied (dark mobile)**: the heading and wrapped two-line explanation are readable, with no retry button and only the exit.
- **Contrast**: white on `rgb(18,107,104)` is about 6.3:1, which passes AA. Secondary text `rgb(194,204,199)` on the dark surface is comfortably readable.
- **Arabic/RTL**: text is right-aligned, the action sits at the start, no text is clipped and nothing overflows at any measured viewport.
- **Width note**: on desktop the card is narrower than the full-width "back to workspace" button. The delta sets no width or margin, so the outer layout already did this. It doesn't block acceptance.
- **Not accepted as proof**: the reference shows a different screen, the staff Time & Attendance table, with no matching error state. My verdict covers only the shared palette, hierarchy and components. The dev badge and the fixture shell are not evidence for this verdict.

## Simpler journey verdict: PASS

- **Unavailable state**: the user goes from two competing secondary links to one obvious in-card recovery plus one clearly secondary exit.
- **Denied state**: the user gets an explanation and a single exit, with no futile retry.
- **No false claims**: the screen claims no success and no speed, and the "still unavailable after reload" result in your report matches what the copy promises.

## Open gates (not closed by this delta)

1. Real Auth and roles. The fixture shows no authorised navigation or real `42501` error from a real session.
2. All valid capture, history and device states for `MobilePunch` (accepted, needs review, review decisions, UTC fallback).
3. The early `!db` branch (no database client). It still renders the old unpadded panel with only the back link. It sits outside `.channel-page`, so these selectors don't reach it. This delta didn't change it and this review didn't cover it.
4. Whole R1/R5/R0–R8 acceptance and full tenant shell composition (header, navigation, tenant teal wrapper in the real app).
5. Real-device check and screen-reader announcement of the error state. Only the keyboard Tab and Enter flow was measured.

I found no concrete defect in this delta.
